user.t:
SECURITY VETTING + RESOLUTION TASK. The user wants "Roo Code" — the AI coding agent (formerly "Roo Cline"). They said "npm install roo code", but Roo Code is primarily a VS Code extension, NOT the npm package `roo` (already confirmed to be an unrelated 2016 koa wrapper). Find the CORRECT, legitimate distribution and vet it. DO NOT run `npm install` on anything, and DO NOT install any VS Code extension. READ-ONLY.

STEPS:
1. Resolve the canonical Roo Code project read-only: find its official GitHub repo (likely RooCodeInc / RooVetGit "Roo-Code", formerly roo-cline), its VS Code Marketplace publisher + extension ID, and its Open VSX listing. Capture: official repo URL, stars/activity, publisher name, exact extension ID (publisher.name), and the official website if any. Confirm which publisher is the REAL one (watch for impersonator/typosquat extensions with similar names).
2. Check npm read-only for any OFFICIAL Roo Code npm/CLI package: `npm view roo-code`, `npm view roocode`, `npm view @roo-code/cli` (and any scope the official repo documents). For each that exists: version, author/maintainers, repository URL (does it match the official repo?), last publish, and the `scripts` field (preinstall/install/postinstall). Flag anything whose repo URL does NOT match the official project as a likely impersonator — do NOT treat it as official.
3. If a legit official npm/CLI package exists, download the TARBALL ONLY (`npm pack <name>` in C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-quarantine, runs no scripts), extract, and inspect package.json scripts + source for lifecycle scripts, obfuscation, child_process exec, arbitrary-URL downloads, env-var/[SENSITIVE_PATH] exfiltration, native binaries, telemetry. NEVER `npm install`.
4. VERDICT, covering BOTH install paths:
   - VS Code extension path: the exact publisher-verified extension ID to install from Marketplace/Open VSX, and how to verify the publisher (so the user doesn't grab an impersonator). Note: installing a VS Code extension is the USER's action in their editor, not an npm command — say so plainly.
   - npm/CLI path: whether an official one exists and whether it's SAFE-TO-INSTALL / SKETCHY-DO-NOT-INSTALL / NO-OFFICIAL-NPM-PACKAGE-EXISTS.
   Flag any impersonator packages/extensions you found.
5. WRITE the write-up to C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-roo-code.md.

Return a concise verdict: the correct official distribution(s), the exact verified extension ID, whether any official npm package exists and its safety, and any impersonators to avoid. Inspection only; never install anything.

handback.t:
VERDICT: Roo Code is a VS Code extension, not an npm package. There is no official npm/CLI install (NO-OFFICIAL-NPM-PACKAGE-EXISTS). The project was shut down on 2026-05-15. Nothing was installed; npm checks were `npm view` and `npm pack --ignore-scripts` (tarballs only).

**Project status (most important)**
- The README of the official repo says "The Roo Code Extension was shut down on May 15th."
- The repo is archived. Last release is v3.54.0 (2026-05-15).
- The maintainers point to ZooCode (community fork, github.com/Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code) and Cline (cline.bot) as alternatives. I did not vet either.
- Canonical repo: https://github.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code (formerly RooVetGit). About 24.3k stars, Apache-2.0. Website: https://roocode.com.

**VS Code extension (official)**
- Exact extension ID: `RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline`. The ID says "roo-cline", not "roo-code".
- Marketplace publisher "Roo Code" has a verified domain, about 2.06M installs, latest 3.54.0.
- Open VSX has the same ID, latest 3.54.0.
- The nightly channel `RooVeterinaryInc.roo-code-nightly` is also official.
- To verify you have the real one, check three things: the exact ID, the verified-domain publisher badge, and that the repo link goes to RooCodeInc/Roo-Code.
- Installing is your action in VS Code (Extensions panel, or `code --install-extension RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline`), not an npm command.
- Because it is shut down and archived, expect no security fixes and possibly dead cloud and billing features. Consider ZooCode or Cline instead.

**npm results**

| Package | Result |
|---|---|
| `roo-code` | 404, does not exist |
| `@roo-code/cli` | 404, does not exist |
| `roo` | unrelated 2016 koa wrapper |
| `roocode` 1.0.0 | Impersonator or squat. Maintainer atikur_rabbi, no repo. The tarball is a placeholder `index.js` that only prints a console message, with no scripts. |
| `roo-cline` 1.0.0 | Impersonator or squat. Maintainer abosena3 (a hackerone.com address), no repo. The tarball contains only `package.json`. The name matches the real extension's internal name, so it looks like a dependency-confusion placeholder. |
| `@roo-code/types` 1.115.0 | Official: roocode.com maintainers, repo matches. It is only a TypeScript types library (depends on zod). No lifecycle scripts; no child_process, eval or network code found in the dist. Safe, but it is not the app. |
| `@roo-code/cloud` 0.29.0 | Official SDK for Roo Code Cloud, which is shut down. Not inspected in depth. |

None of the inspected packages have preinstall, install or postinstall scripts.

**Avoid**
- npm: `roocode`, `roo-cline`, `roo`.
- Marketplace repackagers with unverified publishers, not audited: `HybridTalentComputing.roo-cline-chinese`, `shengsuan-cloud.roo-vibecoding`, `idenworks.roo-otto`, `BakeryInc.bakery-roo-cline`, `felikspeegel.roo-cline-besiege`, `Makehub.makehub`, `ai-henryalps.roo-code-lts` (self-described "Unofficial", updated 2026-09-22), `mayalabs.roo-cline-with-cli`.

Write-up: C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-roo-code.md. Extracted tarballs are in C:\Users\mariu\experiments\vet-quarantine (x1, x2, x3).
